# Demo cohort (synthetic data, for trying the GUI only)

[**English**](README.md) | [**简体中文**](README.zh-CN.md)

This folder lets you try the **Import results** button in the GUI. It contains
**no real subject data**: every number is generated by
`examples/make_demo_cohort.py` with a fixed random seed, and the subject IDs
(`demoA_01`, `demoB_02`, …) are made up. Use it to get familiar with the
interface; **do not use it for any analysis and do not treat it as a reference
for real results**.

---

## How to use it

1. Open ALPSbox and go to the **QC** page.
2. Click **Import results** and choose `demo_synthetic_summary.csv` in this folder.
3. If the results table already has rows, they are merged by subject ID;
   non-conflicting IDs are kept.
4. QC statistics and the per-subject table are re-computed immediately.
5. **Double-click any row** to plot that subject's motion traces on the right.

Step 5 works because each subject also has a sub-folder with the raw eddy output:

```
demo_synthetic_cohort/
  demo_synthetic_summary.csv      <- import this file
  demoA_01/
    eddy_out.eddy_movement_rms    <- motion trace (two columns per volume)
    eddy_out.eddy_outlier_report  <- positions of the red outlier bands
  demoA_02/
  ...
```

The program remembers the CSV's folder and looks for those two files under
`folder/subject_id`. With your own data, put the summary CSV one level above
the per-subject folders.

---

## What this demo shows

Ten subjects in two groups (`groupA` / `groupB`), constructed to produce four
different QC outcomes:

| Subject | Situation | Actual grade |
|---|---|---|
| `demoA_01/02/04`, `demoB_01/03/05` | normal | pass (6 subjects) |
| `demoA_03` | several clear jolts in volumes 9–12 and 26–28 (jitter 0.156 / 0.847 mm), large drift | check |
| `demoA_05` | slow accumulating drift (1.13 / 2.13 mm), normal jitter | info (drift) |
| `demoB_02` | registration failure (`r_wm` 0.875), ALPS consequently low | fail |
| `demoB_04` | many outlier slices (23 of 40 volumes) | check |

Total: 6 pass, 1 info, 2 check, 1 fail.

After importing, use the **Pass / Check / Fail** filters to verify the grading.
`demoA_03` is the clearest example for the motion traces: the jitter spikes are
obvious in the plot.

---

## About the `group` column

The tool itself **does not assume any cohort structure**. The grouping used by
the scatter plot is chosen in the scatter window:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| By ID prefix (default) | take the first segment before `_`, `-` or `.`; `demoA_01` → `demoA` |
| Use the `group` column | read the `group` field from the data; the demo CSV uses `groupA` / `groupB` |
| No grouping | plot everything as one series |

This CSV has a `group` column, so all three options can be tried. With your own
data, any ID naming works as long as each ID has a segment that represents the
group, or simply add a `group` column.

> Note: this tool only computes **per-subject ALPS values and QC**; group
> comparisons are a downstream analysis and are outside the scope of this tool
> (the `group` column is only used for the scatter plot's display grouping).

---

## Regenerating the data

```bash
python3 examples/make_demo_cohort.py
```

The random seed is fixed in the script (`20261023`), so the same seed always
produces the same output. Change the seed or the `SUBJECTS` list for a
different combination.

---

## File format

CSV columns (order does not matter; missing columns are left empty):

```
subject, status, group,
ALPS_L, ALPS_R, ALPS_mean,
r_wm, n_L_proj, n_R_proj, n_L_asso, n_R_asso,
rms_abs_mean, rms_abs_max, rms_rel_mean, rms_rel_max,
n_outlier, n_vol, method, seconds, finished_at
```

Column names are case-insensitive (`ALPS_L` and `alps_L` are both accepted) and
`subject` may also be called `id`.

`eddy_out.eddy_movement_rms` follows the raw FSL eddy output format: one row per
volume, the first column is the absolute displacement relative to volume 1 and
the second is the displacement relative to the previous volume, in millimetres.
The real files from a processed subject can be substituted directly.
